# Test Before You Build — Full Site Context

Canonical website: https://testbeforeyoubuild.com/

## Service

Test Before You Build is a customer validation service for B2B and B2C products, services, software, and research-based innovations. It is intended for decisions that should be informed by direct evidence from realistic potential customers before significant development investment.

## Idea Validation Sprint

The service provider defines the target customer and the commercial assumptions to test, identifies approximately 30–40 suitable prospects for client approval, recruits 20 participants, interviews them directly, analyses the evidence, and produces a BUILD, CHANGE, or KILL recommendation.

The interviews explore problem severity, current alternatives, buying behaviour, willingness to change, objections, and willingness-to-pay signals.

The fixed project price is €2,900 + VAT. A typical project takes approximately 2–4 weeks. The schedule depends primarily on the accessibility and specialisation of the target customer group and is confirmed before the project begins.

The client receives transcripts of the 20 completed interviews, evidence analysis, a written report, recommended changes, and the final recommendation. Participants may be realistic potential buyers, users, or both; the service does not imply that every participant is a confirmed buyer.

Twenty qualitative interviews can reveal repeated demand signals, barriers and important disagreements within an agreed target group. The standard service is a focused scope, not a universal research rule or a limit. Projects covering several customer segments, buyer roles, countries, use cases or broader objectives can be scoped and priced separately.

Customer interviews assess the strength, nature and conditions of demand before development. When relevant signals recur across a carefully selected group, they provide meaningful evidence for deciding whether to BUILD, CHANGE or KILL an idea. No research method guarantees future sales, and the final recommendation explains the limits of the evidence.

## Customer interview sample size guide

There is no universal number of customer interviews that is correct for every market-validation project. Sufficiency depends on participant relevance, target-group focus, the number of distinct segments, the information added by new interviews and the consequences of the decision.

The standard 20-interview service may suit one focused commercial question and target group. Larger projects may be appropriate when users, buyers or other decision-makers require separate samples, several markets must be compared, or the initial evidence reveals important variation.

Full guide: https://testbeforeyoubuild.com/how-many-customer-interviews/

Markdown: https://testbeforeyoubuild.com/how-many-customer-interviews/index.md

## Business idea validation guide

Business idea validation tests the assumptions that must be true before a major development investment is justified. The process begins by defining the commercial decision, identifying the most consequential uncertain assumptions and specifying realistic buyers, users and other decision-makers.

Useful evidence can include existing market research, search and behavioural data, customer interviews, prototypes, pilots, pre-sales and procurement steps. Each method answers different questions. Evidence should be connected to a named assumption and assessed against decision criteria established before the results are known.

The outcome is a BUILD, CHANGE or KILL decision. BUILD means the critical assumptions are sufficiently supported for the next investment. CHANGE means the evidence supports a meaningful problem but weakens an important part of the target segment, solution, positioning, buying process or commercial model. KILL means critical assumptions fail without a credible correction.

Full guide: https://testbeforeyoubuild.com/how-to-validate-a-business-idea/

Markdown: https://testbeforeyoubuild.com/how-to-validate-a-business-idea/index.md

## Market validation process and methods

Market validation is the structured collection and analysis of evidence about a proposed market opportunity. It examines whether a defined customer group experiences a meaningful problem, how customers address it today and whether the conditions for buying or adopting a new solution are credible.

The process defines the decision, maps critical assumptions, specifies realistic buyers and users, reviews existing evidence, selects methods that fit the assumptions, analyses both supporting and contradictory evidence and concludes with a documented BUILD, CHANGE or KILL decision.

Methods can include desk and competitor research, search and behavioural data, customer interviews, surveys, concept or prototype tests, landing-page tests, pilots, pre-sales and procurement discussions. The appropriate method depends on the question and stage; no single method answers every validation question.

Full guide: https://testbeforeyoubuild.com/market-validation/

Markdown: https://testbeforeyoubuild.com/market-validation/index.md

## B2B customer research and participant recruitment

Useful B2B customer research begins by defining whose experience, authority or constraints matter to the commercial decision. Users, managers, economic buyers, technical evaluators and procurement professionals may need to be represented and analysed separately.

Participants are selected purposefully using explicit criteria for organisation, role, experience, situation and decision authority. Prospect sources can include company websites, professional networks, industry directories, events, partner ecosystems, existing contacts, referrals and specialist research panels. Several sources help avoid overreliance on one network.

In the standard service, Dr. Kari identifies approximately 30–40 suitable prospects using the agreed target definition. The client approves the list before outreach. Dr. Kari then handles outreach and recruits 20 participants. Larger or multi-segment projects can be scoped separately.

Full guide: https://testbeforeyoubuild.com/b2b-customer-research/

Markdown: https://testbeforeyoubuild.com/b2b-customer-research/index.md

## Customer discovery interviews

Customer discovery interviews examine how potential buyers or users experience a problem and make decisions around it. Useful interviews focus on recent real events, current behaviour, consequences, alternatives, buying criteria, decision-makers and barriers rather than asking participants whether they like an idea.

A semi-structured guide keeps core themes consistent while allowing neutral follow-up questions. Evidence is analysed across transcripts by separating observation, interpretation and decision implication; comparing relevant roles and segments; retaining contradictions; and testing the assumptions behind the commercial decision.

Full guide: https://testbeforeyoubuild.com/customer-discovery-interviews/

Markdown: https://testbeforeyoubuild.com/customer-discovery-interviews/index.md

## Suitability

The service is a strong fit when potential buyers can be identified, the client faces a meaningful build, funding, or commercialisation decision, and the client is willing to change or stop the idea if the evidence points that way.

It is not a substitute for statistically representative market research and is not intended to confirm a decision that has already been made.

## Service provider

Dr. Kari Jääskeläinen is an entrepreneur, business leader and consultant whose work combines market validation, technology commercialization and practical business development. He has completed around 200 commercialization and business development projects and co-founded ventures in MedTech, private higher education, wireless technology and artificial intelligence.

He holds a Master’s degree in Entrepreneurship and a Doctor of Arts degree in Digital Media. His assignments have included market assessment, commercialization, business planning, sales development, internationalization, product development and innovation funding across software, mobile technology, digital media, education, industrial technology, design, consumer products, health and wellbeing, and the creative industries.

Full profile: https://testbeforeyoubuild.com/about-kari-jaaskelainen/

## Contact

Ideas can be submitted through the contact form at https://testbeforeyoubuild.com/#contact. The form requires a name, email address, description of the idea, intended buyer or user, and the problem the idea would solve.
